model.label: Housing affordability · illustrative city

parameters.label: Initial housing stock
parameters.description: Usable homes at year zero; includes vacant homes.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

parameters.label: Initial households
parameters.description: Households seeking homes at year zero; unmet demand is retained.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

parameters.label: Initial median monthly rent
parameters.description: Illustrative starting monthly gross rent, not a measured local estimate.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

parameters.label: Initial household income
parameters.description: Annual median household income; low-income households are modeled at 55% of this value.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

parameters.label: Household formation / population growth
parameters.description: Household formation rate excluding net migration; fixed household size approximation.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

parameters.label: Net migration
parameters.description: Additional proportional household growth from net migration.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

parameters.label: Real wage growth
parameters.description: Real income trend; economic growth and unemployment also affect income.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

parameters.label: Real economic growth
parameters.description: Affects real income, development demand, and employment.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

parameters.label: Unemployment rate
parameters.description: Starting labor-market stress; raises low-income rent burden and lowers development demand.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

parameters.label: Financing interest rate
parameters.description: Financing costs reduce feasible private starts; not an endogenous monetary model.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

parameters.label: Construction cost per home
parameters.description: Constant-dollar base construction cost; inflation erodes fixed nominal program purchasing power.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

parameters.label: Cost inflation
parameters.description: Construction cost inflation relative to fixed annual program appropriations; rent and income metrics remain in base-year dollars.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

parameters.label: Annual construction capacity
parameters.description: Physical maximum annual starts before labor, cost, and policy constraints.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

parameters.label: Construction duration
parameters.description: Delay from permitted start to completion; projects remain in a tracked pipeline.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

parameters.label: Permitting delay
parameters.description: Time in the permit queue; lowers approvals and delays completions.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

parameters.label: Allowed density multiplier
parameters.description: Land/zoning entitlement capacity relative to current policy; phase-in applies only to policy changes.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

parameters.label: Affordable construction appropriation
parameters.description: Annual public appropriation for a 35% construction cost contribution; only feasible starts draw funds.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

parameters.label: Housing voucher appropriation
parameters.description: Annual rental assistance appropriation; capped at eligible households' rental costs.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

parameters.label: Policy adoption / compliance
parameters.description: Fraction of policy changes implemented, after administrative resistance.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

parameters.label: Policy implementation delay
parameters.description: Delay before policy changes begin a 12-month phase-in; current-policy building continues.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

parameters.label: Administrative resistance
parameters.description: Reduces delivered adoption and delays the phase-in of policy changes.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

parameters.label: Budget delivered
parameters.description: Share of appropriations actually available; combines multiplicatively with stress cuts.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

parameters.label: Annual housing loss
parameters.description: Fraction of existing homes lost each year to demolition or retirement.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

parameters.label: Rent response to vacancy gap

parameters.boundary: Illustrative metropolitan rental market; constant-dollar budgets, monthly stock-flow accounting.

metrics.boundary: Exploratory model output; not an observed forecast.

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

metrics.boundary: Exploratory model output; not an observed forecast.

metrics.boundary: Exploratory model output; not an observed forecast.

metrics.label: Displacement risk proxy

metrics.boundary: Exploratory model output; not an observed forecast.

metrics.label: Cumulative completed homes

metrics.boundary: Exploratory model output; not an observed forecast.

limitations: Synthetic illustrative metropolitan model, not empirically calibrated or a causal forecast. Default city values and behavioral coefficients are assumptions.
Monthly housing stock-flow accounting with permit/construction queues; no household agents, geography, tenure, land prices, or spatial spillovers.
Homelessness, displacement, employment, commute, and tax outputs are stylized proxies, not measured counts or estimated probabilities.
Migration and household formation are exogenous; no migration response to cheaper housing. Density can increase available development but not physical construction capacity.
Public spending is partial incremental program cost. Rent/income use base-year dollars; cost inflation changes purchasing power of fixed appropriations. No debt, discounting, or full public budget.
Random shocks and uncertainty express model assumptions. Ensemble percentiles are scenario spread, not confidence intervals or validated predictive probabilities.
Historical data must match geography, units, observation period, and availability cutoff. National vacancy data do not calibrate an illustrative city's local policy effects.

Building project delays, overruns, cancellation, commercial home-equivalent capacity, and occupancy are synthetic assumptions. Project subsidy is a separate fixed award; private owners absorb overruns. Project-specific affordable units are recorded without a separate tenure/rent-control model.
model.boundary: Metropolitan housing market, base-year dollars, incremental policy budget

source.label: HBL illustrative city assumptions; not empirical calibration

model.description: Exploratory demand, construction-pipeline, budget, and rent stock-flow model.
